# Car Selection Parallel Coordinates Dataset

## Overview
A dataset of 25 car models spanning SUVs, sedans, and electric vehicles, each rated across seven consumer-relevant performance dimensions on a normalized 0–100 scale (higher is better). Designed for multi-dimensional comparison via parallel coordinates.

## Data Source

### cars
- **model** (string): Car model name, 25 unique entries
- **type** (categorical): Vehicle category — one of "SUV" (9 models), "Sedan" (8 models), or "Electric" (8 models)
- **price_score** (integer, 18–88): Affordability score; higher means more affordable
- **fuel_efficiency** (integer, 28–95): Combined fuel/energy efficiency rating
- **power** (integer, 35–95): Engine/motor performance score
- **safety** (integer, 60–92): Composite crash-test and active-safety rating
- **interior_space** (integer, 42–95): Cabin and cargo volume score
- **resale_value** (integer, 35–92): Projected 5-year value retention score
- **emission_rating** (integer, 25–98): Environmental cleanliness score; electric vehicles score near-maximum

## Data Notes
- All scores are normalized to a 0–100 scale for cross-dimension comparability
- Price score is inverted (higher = more affordable) so that "up" is always "better" on every axis
- Electric vehicles uniformly score 98 on emission_rating, reflecting zero tailpipe emissions
- No single model scores in the top 3 across all seven dimensions simultaneously
- Scores are illustrative estimates based on publicly available consumer review aggregates, not official test results

import json
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

# Load data
with open("/app/benchmark/source_data.json") as f:
    source = json.load(f)

cars = source["cars"]["data"]
dimensions = source["cars"]["dimensions"]

# Friendly axis labels
dim_labels = {
    "price_score": "Price\n(Affordability)",
    "fuel_efficiency": "Fuel\nEfficiency",
    "power": "Power",
    "safety": "Safety",
    "interior_space": "Interior\nSpace",
    "resale_value": "Resale\nValue",
    "emission_rating": "Emission\nRating",
}

# Color scheme — business, professional, accessible
type_colors = {
    "SUV": "#D97706",       # amber/gold
    "Sedan": "#2563EB",     # blue
    "Electric": "#059669",  # emerald green
}
type_alpha = 0.45
type_lw = 1.6

# Find top performer per dimension
top_per_dim = {}
for dim in dimensions:
    best_val = -1
    best_model = ""
    for car in cars:
        if car[dim] > best_val:
            best_val = car[dim]
            best_model = car["model"]
    top_per_dim[dim] = best_model

# Build data arrays
models = [c["model"] for c in cars]
types = [c["type"] for c in cars]
data = np.array([[c[d] for d in dimensions] for c in cars])

# Create figure
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(16, 8.5), dpi=150)
fig.patch.set_facecolor("#FAFAFA")
ax.set_facecolor("#FAFAFA")

x = np.arange(len(dimensions))

# Draw polylines grouped by type for legend ordering
for vtype in ["SUV", "Sedan", "Electric"]:
    color = type_colors[vtype]
    for i, car in enumerate(cars):
        if car["type"] != vtype:
            continue
        vals = [car[d] for d in dimensions]
        is_top = any(car["model"] == top_per_dim[d] for d in dimensions)
        ax.plot(
            x, vals,
            color=color,
            alpha=0.55 if not is_top else 0.85,
            linewidth=1.5 if not is_top else 2.8,
            solid_capstyle="round",
            zorder=2 if not is_top else 4,
        )

# Highlight top performers with markers
for dim_idx, dim in enumerate(dimensions):
    top_model = top_per_dim[dim]
    for car in cars:
        if car["model"] == top_model:
            color = type_colors[car["type"]]
            ax.scatter(
                [dim_idx], [car[dim]],
                s=120, color=color, edgecolors="white",
                linewidths=2, zorder=5,
            )
            ax.annotate(
                car["model"],
                xy=(dim_idx, car[dim]),
                xytext=(8, 10),
                textcoords="offset points",
                fontsize=7, fontweight="bold",
                color=color,
                bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.25", facecolor="white", edgecolor=color, alpha=0.85),
                zorder=6,
            )
            break

# Draw axis lines and labels
for i, dim in enumerate(dimensions):
    ax.axvline(x=i, color="#CBD5E1", linewidth=1.2, zorder=1)
    ax.text(i, -8, dim_labels[dim], ha="center", va="top",
            fontsize=9.5, fontweight="semibold", color="#334155",
            linespacing=1.15)

# Y-axis formatting
ax.set_ylim(-15, 108)
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, len(dimensions) - 0.5)
ax.set_yticks([0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100])
ax.set_yticklabels(["0", "20", "40", "60", "80", "100"], fontsize=9, color="#64748B")
ax.yaxis.grid(True, color="#E2E8F0", linewidth=0.7, zorder=0)
ax.set_ylabel("Normalized Score (0–100, higher is better)", fontsize=10, color="#475569", labelpad=10)

# Remove x-axis ticks
ax.set_xticks([])

# Remove top and right spines
ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["bottom"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["left"].set_color("#CBD5E1")

# Title
ax.set_title(
    "Car Selection: No Single Model Dominates All Dimensions",
    fontsize=16, fontweight="bold", color="#1E293B", pad=20,
)
ax.text(
    0.5, 1.02,
    "Every vehicle type excels in some areas but trades off in others — different models lead on different axes",
    transform=ax.transAxes, ha="center", fontsize=10.5, color="#64748B",
)

# Legend
legend_handles = [
    Line2D([0], [0], color=type_colors["SUV"], linewidth=2.5, alpha=0.8, label="SUV (9 models)"),
    Line2D([0], [0], color=type_colors["Sedan"], linewidth=2.5, alpha=0.8, label="Sedan (8 models)"),
    Line2D([0], [0], color=type_colors["Electric"], linewidth=2.5, alpha=0.8, label="Electric (8 models)"),
    Line2D([0], [0], marker="o", color="white", markerfacecolor="#64748B",
           markersize=8, markeredgecolor="white", markeredgewidth=1.5,
           label="Top performer on axis"),
]
legend = ax.legend(
    handles=legend_handles, loc="upper center",
    bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.10), ncol=4, frameon=True,
    fancybox=True, shadow=False, fontsize=9.5,
    edgecolor="#CBD5E1", facecolor="white",
)

# Annotation: trade-off callout between power and fuel efficiency
mid_x = (x[1] + x[2]) / 2
ax.annotate(
    "Power ↔ Efficiency\ntrade-off zone",
    xy=(mid_x, 45), fontsize=8, fontstyle="italic",
    color="#94A3B8", ha="center",
    bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", facecolor="#F8FAFC", edgecolor="#E2E8F0"),
)

# Footer note
fig.text(
    0.5, 0.01,
    "Data: Normalized scores (0–100, higher = better)  |  Price score reflects affordability (higher = more affordable)  |  ● = top scorer on that axis",
    ha="center", fontsize=8, color="#94A3B8",
)

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.04, 1, 0.97])
plt.savefig("/app/output/result.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight", facecolor=fig.get_facecolor())
print("Chart saved to /app/output/result.png")
